title: Simplified Aircraft Motion Test
learningObjectives: Apply a=F_net/m to relate net force and mass to acceleration in one dimension
Predict the sign and magnitude of acceleration from unbalanced thrust and drag
Identify zero net force with zero acceleration for balanced flight

explanations.text: Thrust greater than drag gives a positive net forward force, and the resulting acceleration is calculated from Newton’s second law as net force divided by mass.

evidence.quote: Similarly, increasing the thrust while the drag is constant will cause the plane to accelerate:
Where a is the acceleration, m is the mass of the aircraft, and F is the net force acting on the aircraft.

explanations.text: Drag greater than thrust gives a negative net force, causing a negative acceleration that slows the aircraft, where net force is thrust minus drag.

evidence.quote: And increasing the drag at a constant thrust will cause the plane to slow down:
The net force is the difference between the opposing forces; lift minus weight, or thrust minus drag.

explanations.text: When opposing forces are balanced the net force is zero, so acceleration is zero and velocity remains constant; unbalanced forces cause motion in the direction of the greater force.
